narration.en: A tutor who teaches in March but is paid in April can show the fee in March or in April. The basis of accounting decides which.
narration.kn: ಮಾರ್ಚ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಪಾಠ ಮಾಡಿ ಏಪ್ರಿಲ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಶುಲ್ಕ ಪಡೆಯುವ ಶಿಕ್ಷಕ ಅದನ್ನು ಯಾವ ತಿಂಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ತೋರಿಸಬೇಕು? ಲೆಕ್ಕಶಾಸ್ತ್ರದ ಆಧಾರ ಇದನ್ನು ನಿರ್ಧರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Under the double entry system both aspects of every transaction are recorded, debit and credit, so the arithmetical accuracy can be checked with a trial balance and a true profit and financial position can be found. The single entry system records only some transactions, usually cash and personal accounts; it is incomplete and unscientific, and is used by some small traders.
body.kn: ದ್ವಿಮುಖ ಪದ್ಧತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರತಿ ವ್ಯವಹಾರದ ಎರಡೂ ಮುಖಗಳನ್ನು ದಾಖಲಿಸಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಏಕಮುಖ ಪದ್ಧತಿ ಅಪೂರ್ಣ ಮತ್ತು ಅವೈಜ್ಞಾನಿಕ.

caption.en: The same year can show two different profits. The cash basis counts only cash received and paid; the accrual basis counts what was earned and incurred, whether or not cash moved.
caption.kn: ಒಂದೇ ವರ್ಷ ಎರಡು ಬೇರೆ ಲಾಭ ತೋರಿಸಬಹುದು. ನಗದು ಆಧಾರ ಪಡೆದ ಮತ್ತು ಪಾವತಿಸಿದ ಹಣವನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ ಎಣಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಸಂಚಯ ಆಧಾರ ಗಳಿಸಿದ ಮತ್ತು ಉಂಟಾದದ್ದನ್ನು ಎಣಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

text.en: Cash basis: only money received and paid
Accrual basis: revenue earned and expenses incurred
Earned but not received {er - rc}   Incurred but not paid {ei - pd}

body.en: Under the cash basis, revenue and expenses are recorded only when cash is received or paid. Under the accrual basis, revenue is recorded when earned and expenses when incurred, whether or not cash has moved, so outstanding and prepaid items are recognised. The accrual basis follows the matching concept and is compulsory for companies under the Companies Act, 2013.
body.kn: ನಗದು ಆಧಾರ: ಹಣ ಬಂದಾಗ ಅಥವಾ ಕೊಟ್ಟಾಗ ಮಾತ್ರ ದಾಖಲೆ. ಸಂಚಿತ ಆಧಾರ: ಗಳಿಸಿದಾಗ ಮತ್ತು ವೆಚ್ಚ ಉಂಟಾದಾಗ ದಾಖಲೆ. ಕಂಪನಿಗಳಿಗೆ ಸಂಚಿತ ಆಧಾರ ಕಡ್ಡಾಯ.

problem.en: In 2024-25 a firm made sales of ₹5,00,000 and received ₹4,20,000 in cash. Expenses incurred were ₹3,10,000, of which ₹2,90,000 was paid. Find the profit under the cash basis and the accrual basis.

steps.en: Cash basis profit = cash received − cash paid = ₹4,20,000 − ₹2,90,000 = ₹1,30,000.
Accrual basis profit = revenue earned − expenses incurred = ₹5,00,000 − ₹3,10,000 = ₹1,90,000.
The difference of ₹60,000 = ₹80,000 still to be received − ₹20,000 still to be paid.
